qs.q: The angle between the plane of the ecliptic and the plane of equator is approximately?
A Rhumb line is:
o: a line on the surface of the earth cutting all meridians at the same angle
any straight line on a lambert projection
a line convex to the nearest pole on a Mercator projection

qs.q: If you want to follow a constant true track value:
o: you must fly a great circle.
you must fly a rhumb line.
you, in most cases, will also fly the shortest possible track.

qs.q: Which of the following differences in latitude will produce the greatest difference between the initial great circle track and the mean great circle track, between two point, which are separated by 15° change of longitude?
qs.ex: Convergency = Δlong × sin mean lat, so the pair with the highest mean latitude (60°N/55°N) gives the biggest difference.

qs.q: Position A is 58°N 030°W and position B is 51°N 020°W. What is the rhumb line bearing from A to B, if the great circle track from A to B, measured at A, is 100° T?
qs.ex: Conversion angle = ½ × Δlong × sin mean lat = 5 × sin 54.5° ≈ 4°. In the northern hemisphere the great circle lies poleward of the rhumb line, so RL = 100 + 4 = 104°T.

qs.q: The countries having a standard time slow on UTC:
o: will often have an earlier standard date than the UTC date.
will generally be located at eastern longitudes.
will generally be located at western longitudes.

qs.q: Isogonic lines connect positions that have:
Compass deviation is defined as the angle between:
o: the horizontal and the total intensity of the earth's magnetic field

qs.q: What is the final position after the following rhumb line tracks and distances have been followed from position 60° 00'N 030° 00'W? South for 360 NM, East for 360 NM, North for 360 NM, West for 360 NM.
qs.ex: South 360 NM → 54°N. East 360 NM at 54°N = 612' of longitude; west 360 NM at 60°N = 720'. Net 108' ≈ 1° 48' west → 031° 48'W.

qs.q: In order to fly from position A (10° 00'N, 030° 00'W) to position B (30° 00'N, 050° 00'W), maintaining a constant true course, it is necessary to fly?
o: A straight line plotted on a Lambert chart.

qs.q: An aircraft departs from position A (09° 10'S 178° 22'W) and flies northward following the meridian for 2750 NM. It then flies westward along the parallel of latitude for 400 NM to position B. The coordinates of position B are?
Position A 45° N, ?° E; position B 45° N, 45° 15'E. Distance A–B = 200 NM, B is to the east of A. What is the longitude of position A?

Two aircraft are flying eastwards around the earth. Aircraft A is flying along the 45°N parallel of latitude and aircraft B along the equator. If aircraft A is flying at a groundspeed of 300 knots, what would be the groundspeed of aircraft B if both aircraft fly once round the Earth in the same journey time?
When correcting a RAS of 150 kt, a TAS of less than 150 kt is obtained. Therefore the:
o: density of the air must be greater than ISA mean sea level air density
allowance has not been made for compressibility
an error must have been made in the calculations
qs.ex: The printed question says 'a TAS of > 150 kt', which makes none of the options right; the source question reads 'less than 150 kt'. TAS below RAS means the air is denser than ISA sea level.

qs.q: The purpose of a compass swing is to?
o: Align the lubber lines with true north.
Confirm the accuracy of the schuler tuning.
Align compass north with magnetic north.

qs.q: A runway in the northern hemisphere is on an agonic line and heading 045 degrees. If an aircraft with zero compass deviation takes off in still air, what will the compass (acceleration) error be?
o: The compass will move to less than 045.
The compass will move to more than 045.

o: Great circle and rhumb line are to the south of the parallel of origin.
Great circle and rhumb line are to the north the parallel of origin.

qs.q: Maximum allowable crosswind component is 20 kt. Runway 06, QDM 063° (M). Wind direction 100° (M). Calculate the maximum allowable wind speed.
qs.ex: The book uses the runway number (060°): angle 40°, so 20 / sin 40° ≈ 31 kt. (With QDM 063°, 20 / sin 37° ≈ 33 kt.)

qs.q: Distance 'Q' to 'R' 2160 NM, Groundspeed 'out' 535 kt, Groundspeed 'back' 585 kt. Safe endurance 6 HR. The distance from 'Q' to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) between 'Q' and 'R' is?
True course A to B = 250°, distance A to B = 315 NM, TAS = 450 kt, W/V = 200°/60 kt, ETD A = 0650 UTC. What is the ETA at B?
qs.ex: Wind 50° off the nose from the left: drift ≈ 6°, GS ≈ 450 cos 6° − 60 cos 50° ≈ 409 kt. 315 / 409 ≈ 46 min → 0736.

qs.q: For a constant Calibrated Airspeed (CAS) and a level flight, a fall in ambient temperature will result in a?
o: Lower True Airspeed (TAS) due to a decrease in air density.
Lower True Airspeed (TAS) due to an increase in air density.
Higher True Airspeed (TAS) due to a decrease in air density.

Distance 'A' to 'B' 2450 NM, Groundspeed 'out' 350 kt, Groundspeed 'back' 385 kt, The time from 'A' to the Point of Equal Time (PET) between 'A' and 'B' is?

At 0430 an aircraft is in level cruise flight at a groundspeed of 350 knots, at FL370, 165 NM from a VOR. It is required to descend at a mean rate of 1800 feet/min, to be at FL80 overhead the VOR. What is the latest time to commence descent, if the mean ground speed in the descent is to be 200 knots?
qs.ex: 29 000 ft at 1800 ft/min = 16.1 min, covering 16.1/60 × 200 ≈ 54 NM. Cruise 165 − 54 = 111 NM at 350 kt = 19 min → start descent at 0449.

qs.q: An aeroplane is to depart from an airfield where the performance limited take-off mass is 89 200 kg. Certificated maximum masses: ramp (taxi) mass 89 930 kg, take-off mass 89 430 kg, landing mass 71 520 kg, zero fuel mass 62 050 kg. Fuel on board at ramp: taxi fuel 600 kg, trip fuel 17 830 kg, contingency, final reserve and alternate 9030 kg. If the Dry Operating Mass is 40 970 kg the traffic load that can be carried on this flight is:
qs.ex: The book treats 62 050 kg as the limiting zero fuel mass: traffic load = 62 050 − 40 970 = 21 080 kg (TOM 89 200 would allow 21 370 kg).

qs.q: An aero plane is performance limited to a landing mass of 54230 kg. The Dry Operating Mass is 35000 kg and the zero fuel mass is 52080 kg. If the take-off mass is 64280 kg the useful load is:
qs.ex: Useful load = TOM − DOM = 64 280 − 35 000 = 29 280 kg.

qs.q: The empty mass of an aero plane, as given in the weighing schedule, is 61300 kg. The operational items (including crew) is given as a mass of 2300 kg. If the take-off mass is 132000 kg (including a useable fuel quantity of 43800 kg) the useful load is
DOM 33 500 kg, payload 7600 kg, MTOW 66 200 kg, taxi fuel 200 kg, tank capacity 16 100 kg. Find the maximum fuel and traffic load that can be carried.
qs.ex: Take-off fuel = tank 16 100 − taxi 200 = 15 900 kg. Traffic = 66 200 − 33 500 − 15 900 = 16 800 kg.

qs.q: An aircraft flies a great circle track from 56° N 070° W to 62° N 110° E. The total distance traveled is?
qs.ex: 070°W and 110°E are on the same great circle through the pole: (90 − 56) + (90 − 62) = 62° × 60 = 3720 NM.

qs.q: On the 27th of February, at 52°S 040°E, sunrise is at 0243 UTC. On the same day, at 52°S 035°W, sunrise is at:
qs.ex: Same latitude, 75° further west = 5 h later: 0243 + 0500 = 0743 UTC.

The distance between two waypoints is 200 NM, To calculate compass heading, the pilot used 2°E magnetic variation instead of 2°W. Assuming that the forecast W/V applied, what will the off track distance be at the second waypoint?
qs.ex: The error is 4°. By the 1 in 60 rule, 200 NM × 4/60 ≈ 13–14 NM off track.

qs.q: In a non-pressurized aircraft, if one or several static pressure ports are damaged, there is an ultimate emergency means for restoring a practically correct static pressure intake?
o: Breaking the rate-of climb indicator glass window.
Slightly opening a window to restore the ambient pressure in the cabin.
Descending as much as possible in order to fly at a pressure as close to 1013.25 hPa as possible.

qs.q: The vertical speed indicator of an aircraft flying at a true airspeed of 100 kt, in a descent with a slope of 3 degrees, indicates?
qs.ex: ROD ≈ GS × 101 × tan 3° ≈ 100 × 101 × 0.052 ≈ 530 ft/min, i.e. about −500 ft/min.

qs.q: The principle used in VOR bearing measurement is:

An aircraft is flying on the true track 090° towards a VOR station located near the equator where the magnetic variation is 15°E. The variation at the aircraft position is 8°E. The aircraft is on VOR radial:
qs.ex: Flying 090°T towards the VOR, the aircraft is due west of it: true bearing from the station 270°. Use the variation at the station: 270 − 15 = 255°.

qs.q: VOR station position N61° E025°, variation 13°E; Estimated position of an aircraft N59° E025°, variation 20°E. What VOR radial is the aircraft on?
qs.ex: The aircraft is due south of the VOR: 180°T − 13°E = 167°.

qs.q: The International Date Line is found on or near the ______. When crossing the date line travelling west, you go into the ______ day:
qs.ex: Book key prints (b). The date line roughly follows the 180° meridian, and travelling westwards across it you move into the next day (for example, leaving Los Angeles on Monday you arrive in Tokyo on Tuesday).
